messages:
Aisha (sec-eng): FYI found a batch of short-lived service tokens in partner ingest logs (staging). guessing ephemeral creds got captured by debug logs. linking the sample: https://internal/links/RED-A-123 :eyes:
Ben (infra): ugh. are these Vault dynamic creds or long-lived SA keys?
Aisha (sec-eng): dynamic, minted by our Vault agent. TTL ~ 15m but some were logged right after issuance. only appears in partner-ingest-staging namespace so blast radius limited.
Carlos (oncall): sec-bot alert flagged a spike in vault/lease/revoke failures around 12:04 UTC. I pulled recent audit log snippet and attached to thread.
sec-bot: Incident detected: vault.audit.invalid_token_count increased by 34 at 2024-11-12T12:04:21Z. Ticket created: #SEC-4879.
Dawn (platform): ok can we confirm which KMS wrapping key was used for transit? if these are wrapped blobs we may need a rewrap step before reissuing.
Aisha (sec-eng): they're Vault dynamic leases; Vault transit is enabled for the token wrapping path. key: projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/vault/cryptoKeys/vault-wrap-1
Ben (infra): good. immediate plan: 1) revoke outstanding leases for the affected role, 2) rotate the Vault issuance role policy (deny partner-ingest namespace), 3) export audit logs for the 1h window to secure S3 for forensic, 4) short maintenance window to rekey/rewrap if necessary.
Aisha (sec-eng): I can run revoke for the role now. command I used in staging: ```vault lease revoke -prefix auth/approle/role/partner-ingest/``` This will nuke current leases for that role.
Carlos (oncall): running it now on staging. will post completion. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Carlos (oncall): done. revoke returned 143 leases revoked. CPU spike on staging vault but healthy now.
Dawn (platform): I'm starting a quick RBAC tweak: temporarily add a deny rule to the approle policy for partner-ingest so new tokens can't be minted from that path while we investigate. patch in terraform then apply. pinging @Ben to approve plan.
Ben (infra): approve. Also schedule a rewrap if audit shows any wrapped blob exposures. If we need to rewrap, we should use the offline-key rotation flow so we don't break existing encrypted backups.
Aisha (sec-eng): Forensic checklist: - snapshot vault audit logs (I exported to s3://sec-forensics/SEC-4879/) - map all approles and issued leases in the 24h window - identify any long-lived refreshers - notify partner security (already DM'd)
Carlos (oncall): audit export started. ETA ~8 minutes.
Dawn (platform): quick KMS Q for infra: if we rotate the KMS cryptoKey, does Vault auto-rewrap existing ciphertext or do we have to call the rewrap API?
Ben (infra): Vault doesn't auto-rewrap. We'll have to call the rewrap API against each ciphertext that used that key. Options: use a small rewrap job that reads ciphertext from metadata store and calls GCP KMS rewrap, or create a transient worker that re-encrypts using new key. Prefer controlled batch with retry.
Aisha (sec-eng): Added a short script to the thread for rewrap pattern (GCP): ```python
# pseudo
k = kms.KeyManagementServiceClient()
resp = k.rewrap_crypto_key_version(name=old_key_name, ciphertext=ciphertext)
# store new ciphertext back in secret metadata
``` Keep minimal scope; we'll only rewrap blobs referenced by the leaked leases.
Carlos (oncall): Also triage note: none of the revoked leases showed activity beyond issuance timestamp in logs. looks like capture was immediate; likely a logging config in partner code. I've asked them to scrub logs and rotate local copies.
Dawn (platform): For the RBAC change I pushed a tf patch: `deny = ["auth/approle/role/partner-ingest/*:create"]` and applied in staging. will prepare PR for prod lockstep after forensics signoff.
Ben (infra): We should rotate the Vault transit key too (create new cryptoKey version) and then run selective rewrap for any customer blobs. I'll own the KMS key rotation.
Aisha (sec-eng): Ownership: - Forensics & audit export: Aisha - RBAC deny & policy change: Dawn - Revoke leases & initial containment: Carlos - KMS key rotation & rewrap job: Ben - Partner comms: Aisha
Carlos (oncall): I've updated ticket #SEC-4879 with the revoke counts, attached audit export link, and noted owner assignments.
Dawn (platform): Partner confirmed they will purge captured logs and rotate any stored tokens. asked them to provide a signed attestation once done.
Ben (infra): Next steps — I'll create a small rewrap worker in infra-job-runner, test on a handful of blobs, then scale. target finish: 6 hours.
Aisha (sec-eng): Heads-up: we'll need to add an audit log retention rule to keep the 24h window for 30d for safety. raising a console change request.
Carlos (oncall): monitoring for abnormal access; no signs of exfil beyond the logs so far.
Dawn (platform): once Ben confirms rewrap job works, I'll revert the deny rule in prod with a canary release of the policy.
Aisha (sec-eng): thanks all. I'll keep partner ops in the loop. please react when you complete your item so I can close the ticket. :white_check_mark:
Ben (infra): completed initial rewrap test on 3 blobs — success. will proceed to batch.
Carlos (oncall): audit export completed and archived.
Dawn (platform): RBAC deny applied to prod in staged canary (10%). watching.
Aisha (sec-eng): final note for postmortem: add a lesson to avoid logging raw tokens at the partner boundary and to prefer token proxies. I'll start the incident doc.
sec-bot: Ticket #SEC-4879 status updated to: containment_in_progress -> tasks_assigned
Aisha (sec-eng): thread complete for now. will reopen if anything changes. :lock:
